overall.summary: Every number in the draft reproduces (214 of 214 claims, 0 prose mismatches). Nothing is refuted. Eight statements are weakened: part-only numbers worded as if they were the model's prediction (Yugoslavia, preschool, state government), the Thailand-born exception to the age step, an unneeded Ireland exclusion, a 49 vs 50 hour threshold, the size of the sex effect, and 'one or two inputs' per part. One flag: the model predicts about 0% for all 29 armed-forces spouses, of whom 55% had a low income.

findings.statement: through it age adds to the chance once it rises above about 46 years; for 26 of the 39073 training people it already acts below that
findings.check: subgroup Thailand-born, and Thailand-born under 46; probe age sweep by country
findings.evidence: The 26 are the Thailand-born, and for them the part works the other way at younger ages: it lowers the score (contribution -2.10 at 22 years, -0.20 at 40; mean -0.97 for the 20 Thailand-born training people under 46, -0.51 for all 26). Only 20 of the 26 are actually under 46. The sentence implies the same risk-raising effect starts earlier. The 10779 count reproduces (20 under 46 + 10759 at 46 or over).

findings.statement: the chance for a typical person born outside Ireland and Thailand is lowest at about 47 years and higher either side (also annotations.ann_124[2], readdown.ann_124.evidence[3])
findings.evidence: Ireland-born follow the same dip as US-born (the age step's contribution is identical; risk 69.7% at 22, lowest 27.5% at 46, 35.1% at 58), so leaving Ireland out is unexplained. US typical: 88.6% at 22, lowest 56.1% at 46 (56.6% at 47), 64.6% at 58, so 'about 47' holds. The wording 'a higher age lowers the chance ... lowest at about 47 and higher either side' mixes a steady fall with a dip.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --sweep age=22,40,44,45,46,47,48,50,58 --sweep native-country=39,21,37

findings.evidence: part contribution 0 up to 46, +0.09 at 47, +0.41 at 50, +1.26 at 58; whole-model 88.6% / 56.1% / 64.6%

findings.statement: Being born in Yugoslavia lowers the chance from about 72% to about 42%, while working for a state government moves it from about 72% to about 71% (also annotations.ann_117, readdown.ann_117, hypothesis_revisions.ann_117)
findings.evidence: Both claims are part-scope (input changed only where this part reads it) but the sentences do not say 'through this part'. The model's own prediction for a typical Yugoslavia-born person is 51.2%, not 42%; for a typical state-government worker it is 78.4%, i.e. the model raises the chance (the weighted sum adds +0.37), the opposite of the impression given. Through this part alone: -1.23 and -0.005 log-odds, which match 42% and 71%.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold typical --sweep native-country=39,41 --sweep workclass=4,7 --wide

findings.statement: A preschool education raises the chance for a typical person with that education (and the education level of 1) from about 72% to about 91% (also annotations.ann_121[1], readdown.ann_121.evidence[1])
findings.evidence: 91% is through this part alone. For the person the sentence describes (preschool, education level 1) the model predicts 99.6%, because the weighted sum adds +3.08 more for the low education level. The sentence reads as the model's prediction.

findings.statement: marriage and sex move the predicted chance by large amounts
findings.evidence: The 72% to 99% 'typical woman' change (+3.37 log-odds) is mostly marital status and household role, which the linked typical woman also changes. Sex alone adds +0.50 log-odds (98.8% to 99.3% among never-married people not in a family; about 72% to 81% at the typical score). The other sentences (blocks[0][3], annotations) disclose the linked inputs and are upheld; this summary sentence attributes a large effect to sex.
commands: uv run python -m explaneat verify probe <T> --hold "where:`marital-status` == '4' and relationship == '1'" --sweep sex=1,0
